posts.text:
Nike paid Tiger Woods $100 million, the richest endorsement deal in sports, and in 2005 his ball froze on the edge of the cup for two seconds with the swoosh staring straight into the camera, and the world only saw it because one man in the CBS truck didn't cut away.

Final round of the 2005 Masters. Tiger was one shot ahead on the 16th.

His ball sat against the rough. He chipped it up the slope and watched it roll back down toward the hole.

It stopped on the lip. Swoosh facing the camera.

Inside the CBS truck, the director decided it was over and called for a close-up of Tiger.

Technical director Norm Patterson didn't cut. He waited.

The ball dropped. The whole world saw it.

A 30-second ad that day cost about $250,000. Those two seconds were worth $16,666 every time a network replayed them. Within four days, Nike had over $1 million in free advertising.

The director's words: "Thank you, Norm."

It was Norm's last Masters. A few months later, he died of a sudden heart attack. He was 45.

Tiger stayed with Nike for 27 years. His deals added up to $660 million.

posts.text:
'EBUBE DIKE,' NIGERIA HAS LOST ONE OF ITS GREATEST THESPIANS 

​It was with deep sorrow that I received the news of the passing of Chief Peter Uwadiegwu Ogugua Edochie, better known as Pete Edochie.

​Chief Edochie was an exceptional actor - one of the progenitors of our vibrant film industry, Nollywood. He was graceful and larger than life, both on the screen and in person.

He was one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians. For decades, he plied his craft, bringing joy, laughter, and charm to many homes.

​I recall his unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s evergreen novel, Things Fall Apart, in the 1980s, and his many brilliant performances afterwards.

Through memorable performances in productions such as Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart, he helped shape the evolution and international visibility of
Nollywood. 

His portrayal of traditional institutions, family structures, African values, and the complexities of human relationships helped project Nigeria's cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences worldwide. 

Pete Edochie was not only an actor; he was also an administrator, broadcaster, and journalist- truly one of our finest. His place in the pantheon of those who shaped the film industry, our common norms, and popular culture remains indisputable.

​As I mourn the passing of this legendary actor, I also reflect on his life. Pete Edochie lived well. He played his part and exited gracefully.

​In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather.

​On behalf of my family and the Federal Government of Nigeria, I extend my condolences to the Edochie family, his friends, associates, and the entire Nigerian film industry.

​May God Almighty grant "Ebube Dike" eternal rest.

​Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR
President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces
Federal Republic of Nigeria.

November 25, 2026

- 2010: Earned 96 points with Real Madrid, a club record at the time, yet still lost the league to Guardiola’s Barcelona!

- 2013: Came within minutes of reaching the Champions League semi finals with Málaga, only for Dortmund to score twice in stoppage time!

- 2014: Won the Premier League and League Cup with Manchester City in his first season, finishing his time in England with 3 trophies in total.

- 2026: Brought Real Betis back to the Champions League after 21 years away, collecting 12 points from a possible 15!

Betis are currently sitting 4th, ahead of Arsenal, Manchester City, Barcelona, Liverpool and Bayern Munich!

Kwajalein Atoll in the Republic of the Marshall Islands has seen a lot of space history, and we had the privilege of seeing it firsthand. We flew over Omelek Island, where @SpaceX first reached orbit with Falcon 1 in 2008. Pretty extraordinary to look down at that launch site and think about everything that’s flown since.

In 2025, @NASA launched two sounding rockets from Kwajalein to study Earth’s upper atmosphere. Two more sounding rocket missions are planned for 2028. This summer, Northrop Grumman’s final Pegasus XL rocket carried Katalyst Space’s LINK robotic servicing spacecraft to orbit.

We also got to see the Ground Based Radar up close and meet some of the incredible individuals behind these missions. Thank you to the @USArmy for showing us around the Atoll, your service, sacrifice, and for the work you do to make these missions possible.
